v1.feedback: The radial breath-pulse reads as a smooth sine wash rather than a true ostinato — try a sharper, more staccato opacity envelope (e.g. a clamped sawtooth or a quantized step function) so the repetition feels rhythmic and percussive, not just ambient breathing. With 16k lines the inner shells merge into an opaque cocoon; thin the catA count by ~30% or widen the void radii so individual threads remain legible near the sphere. The warm-cream palette and Shiota convergence geometry are strong, but the piece would land harder if the ostinato rhythm were audible in the motion — right now it could be any slow pulse, not a stubborn repeating figure.

v2.feedback: The ostinato concept lands as rhythmic breathing/pulse on the threads and sphere, which is a reasonable read, but the Shiota-installation framing feels like a fresh composition rather than a visible mutation of seed_channel c9v — chain mode should leave structural DNA of the parent legible. Thinning convergence threads to 38% and adding voids helps legibility, but the 16k line count still risks visual noise at distance; consider dropping to ~10k with thicker linewidth to keep individual filaments readable. The quantizeAngle snapping near the sphere is a smart touch that reinforces the repetitive-pattern idea — lean into that more by making the angular grid visually distinct (slight color or opacity shift on snapped vs free threads) so the ostinato structure reads in 2 seconds rather than requiring study.
